It appears that upon urgency being shown in the matter by the Appellant, the Commission took up the petition for hearing on 12[th] July, 2018 and upon hearing all the parties passed an interim order to the following effect :- 9. On behalf of Respondent Nos. 2 & 8, it is contended that the instant appeal has been filed against the order dated 13[th] December, 2018 of the Commission vide which the Commission refused to review/modify its earlier interim order dated 12[th] July, 2018 and, therefore, the same is not maintainable at all. It is submitted that the Appellant ought to have assailed the main interim order dated 12[th] July, 2018 and that having not been done, instant appeal is not maintainable. It is also contended that having chosen not to assail the interim order dated 12[th] July, 2018 before this Tribunal, it was incumbent upon the Appellant to await the final decision of the Commission on the petition and to assail the final decision before this Tribunal by way of an appeal, if so advised. 10. It is contended on behalf of the Appellant on this aspect that impugned order dated 13[th] December, 2018 of the Commission is the final order as no further proceedings were conducted by the Commission thereafter in petition and the petition was disposed off. It is submitted that the said order dated 13[th] December, 2018, being the final order of the Commission on the petition, is assailable by way of an appeal before this Tribunal. 13. At the outset, we may note that having regard to the controversy raised by the Learned Counsels during course of hearing of the appeal as to whether the impugned order dated 13[th] December, 2018 of the Commission was an interlocutory order or a final order disposing off the petition, we had directed the Commission to file an affidavit in this regard. An affidavit dated 4[th] August, 2025 has been filed by the Commission in pursuance to these directions issued by us wherein it has been stated that as per the record maintained in the office of the Commission, the status of the Petition No. 1328 of 2018 is marked as “Disposed”. order dated 13[th] December, 2018, no further hearing was conducted by the Commission in the said petition. However, that alone does not make the order dated 13[th] December, 2018 a final order on the petition thereby disposing it off. In order to ascertain whether an order passed by the Commission is an interlocutory order or a final order, the tone and tenor of the order as well as the circumstances in which the order is passed, are to be seen and analyzed. 16. Having regard to these circumstances in which the Commission passed the impugned order dated 13[th] December, 2018 and the language used therein one cannot by any stretch of imagination, say that it is a final order disposing off the petition. Manifestly, in this order, the Commission was dealing with only additional statement of facts filed by the Appellant wherein prayer had been made for modification of the order dated 12[th] July, 2018 by holding the effective date of payment of transmission charges by UPPTCL/UPPCL as 27[th] July, 2017. It is for this reason that in the concluding paragraph No. 4 of the order, the Commission has held that the _“additional submissions are rejected and the order dated 12[th] July, 2018 will continue_ ”. It is evident that the Commission has not taken up the petition for final disposal and it was only dealing with the additional statement of facts filed by the Appellant. The language of the order itself, particularly used in concluding paragraph No. 4 of the order, would clearly indicate that something more needed to be done in the petition and further proceedings were to be conducted therein. It is amply clear that the said order dated 13[th] December, 2018 is only an interlocutory order passed on the additional statement of facts filed by the Appellant and which cannot be treated as a final order on the petition merely for the reasons that petition was never taken up for disposal thereafter and the status of the petition in the records of the Commission has been shown as “Disposed”. 17. Coming to the aspect of maintainability of the appeal as having been filed against the order dated 13[th] December, 2018 of the Commission. As already noted hereinabove, in the said order, the Commission was only dealing with the request of the Appellant to review/modify interim order dated 12[th] July, 2018. Since, the said request of the Appellant for review/modification of the interim order dated 12[th] July, 2018 stood rejected, the order is clearly not appealable in view of the provisions of Order 47 Rules 7 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. It is elementary that an order rejecting the prayer for review/modification of an earlier order is not appealable at all. 18. Further, even if it is assumed for the sake of arguments that we are convinced by the grounds taken in the instant appeal by the Appellant and set aside the order dated 13[th] December, 2018, in that case also, the 19. Having regard to the above noted facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the considered opinion that the instant appeal is not maintainable. The same stands dismissed as such. However, we hasten to add that the Commission has erroneously shown and treated the Appellant’s petition No. 1328 of 2018 as “Disposed” in its records whereas it had never been taken up for final disposal. Accordingly, we direct the Commission to take up the petition for final disposal forthwith and pass a final order after affording the parties a reasonable opportunity of hearing. Since the petition has remained on the docket of the Commission since the year 2018 without being finally disposal off, we further direct the Commission to pass a final order within two months from the date of this judgement. are at liberty to approach this Tribunal again by way of an appeal if feeling aggrieved by the final order to be passed by the Commission.
title: South East U.P. Power Transmission Company Limited VERSUS Uttar Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission & Ors
